Fast Weighted Cumulative Exposure Model

Source: R/wceGPU.R
wceGPU.Rd

Fits a weighted cumulative exposure (WCE) model on the GPU (or the CPU). Only point estimates are computed: call bootstrap() on the result for bootstrap confidence intervals, and inspect it with summary() and plot().

wceGPU(data, nknots, cutoff, constrained = FALSE, aic = FALSE, id,
       event, start, stop, expos, covariates = NULL,
       confint = 0.95, x = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'wceGPU'
summary(object, allres = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'wceGPU'
plot(x, ..., hist.covariates = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'wceGPU'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, ..., digits = 3)

Arguments

data

Data frame in counting-process (long) format, with one row per subject and time unit.

nknots

Number of interior knots of the cubic spline that models the weight function. With several values (e.g. 1:3), one model is fitted per value and the one with the smallest information criterion (see aic) is kept; best.nknots and the *.grid components of the result describe all the candidates.

cutoff

Length, in time units, of the exposure history that affects the hazard: the weight function is estimated for lags 0 to cutoff - 1 (the cutoff columns of WCEmat), and older exposures have no effect.

constrained

Shape constraint on the weight function. FALSE (default): none. "Right" (or "R"): it decreases smoothly to zero at the oldest lag. "Left" (or "L"): it is zero at lag 0, so the current exposure has no effect.

aic

Logical. Information criterion used to choose among the nknots candidates and reported in info.criterion: the AIC if TRUE, the BIC if FALSE (default). Both equal \(-2 \log(PL) + k p\), with \(PL\) the partial likelihood and \(p\) the number of estimated parameters; \(k = 2\) for the AIC and \(k = \log(d)\), with \(d\) the number of events, for the BIC (Volinsky and Raftery, 2000).

id

Name of the column of data that identifies the subjects.

event

Name of the column of data with the event indicator, coded 1 (event) or 0 (no event).

start

Name of the column of data with the start time of each interval (the time argument of survival::Surv()).

stop

Name of the column of data with the end time of each interval (the time2 argument of survival::Surv()).

expos

Name of the column of data with the exposure.

covariates

Character vector with the names of the columns of data to adjust for. NULL (default): no adjustment.

confint

Level of the bootstrap confidence intervals computed by bootstrap() (default 0.95).

x

For wceGPU(): logical. If TRUE, the columns of data used by the model (id, event, start, stop, expos and covariates) are stored in the result, as data. Required by bootstrap(), which resamples exactly the data the model was fitted on. For plot(): a wceGPU object.

...

For wceGPU(): device ("cpu" or "cuda"; default: the GPU if one is available) and double_precision (TRUE, the default, for 64-bit floats; FALSE for 32-bit floats, faster on most GPUs). For the methods: not used.

object

A wceGPU object.

allres

Logical. If TRUE, summary() prints every candidate number of knots that was tried, with its partial log-likelihood and information criterion, instead of the summary of the selected model (default FALSE).

hist.covariates

Logical. If TRUE and bootstrap() was called on the model, plot() also draws, for each covariate, the histogram of its bootstrap coefficients (default FALSE).

parm

Covariates whose coefficients get a confidence interval, as numbers or names. Missing (default): all of them.

level

Confidence level of confint() (default 0.95).

digits

Number of significant digits of the levels in the column names of confint() (default 3).

Value

wceGPU() returns an object of class wceGPU: a list that describes the selected model, i.e. the candidate in nknots that minimizes the information criterion. Its main components are:

  • WCEmat: matrix with one row and cutoff columns, the estimated weight function.

  • beta.hat.covariates, se.covariates: one-row matrices with the estimated coefficients of the covariates and their standard errors.

  • est, SED: one-row matrices with the estimated spline coefficients and their standard errors.

  • vcovmat: list holding the variance-covariance matrix of all the coefficients (covariates, then spline coefficients).

  • knotsmat: one-row matrix with the knots of the spline basis.

  • loglik, info.criterion, nevents: partial log-likelihood, information criterion (the BIC, or the AIC if aic = TRUE) and number of events.

  • best.nknots: the selected number of interior knots. nknots.grid, info.criterion.grid and loglik.grid give the candidates and the information criterion and partial log-likelihood obtained for each.

  • data: with x = TRUE, the columns of data used by the model.

After bootstrap(), the object also contains:

  • WCEmat_bootstrap, bootstrap_beta.hat.covariates: matrices with one row per bootstrap replicate, for the weight function and for the coefficients of the covariates.

  • WCEmat_CI, coef_CI: two-row matrices with their lower and upper percentile confidence limits, at level confint.

  • bootstrap.best.nknots: the number of knots selected in each replicate.

  • bootstrap_est, est_CI: the same for the spline coefficients, only when a single nknots value is given.

summary() and plot() are called for their side effects (printing the model, plotting the weight function) and return NULL invisibly. confint() returns a matrix with one row per covariate and two columns: the lower and upper confidence limits of its coefficient, based on the normal approximation.

Details

At each time \(t\), the exposure enters the Cox model through its weighted cumulative exposure over the last cutoff time units, $$WCE(t) = \sum_{u=0}^{cutoff-1} w(u) X(t-u),$$ where \(X(t-u)\) is the exposure \(u\) time units before \(t\). The weight function \(w\) is a cubic spline with nknots interior knots. \(WCE(t)\) is therefore a linear combination of spline-weighted exposure histories, which enter a Cox proportional hazards model as time-dependent covariates, together with covariates. Their estimated coefficients give \(w\), returned in WCEmat.

References

Sylvestre MP, Abrahamowicz M. Flexible modeling of the cumulative effects of time-dependent exposures on the hazard. Stat Med. 2009 Nov 30;28(27):3437-53. doi:10.1002/sim.3701

Sylvestre M (2025). WCE: Weighted Cumulative Exposure Models. R package version 1.0.4. doi:10.32614/CRAN.package.WCE . The reference implementation of the method: wceGPU() follows its interface, and its results are tested against it.

Volinsky CT, Raftery AE (2000). Bayesian information criterion for censored survival models. Biometrics, 56(1), 256-262. doi:10.1111/j.0006-341X.2000.00256.x

See also

bootstrap()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Dataset
drugdata <- WCE::drugdata

# WCE model, point estimate only
wce_gpu <- wceGPU(data = drugdata, nknots = 1, cutoff = 90, id = "Id",
                  event = "Event", start = "Start", stop = "Stop",
                  expos = "dose", covariates = c("age", "sex"),
                  constrained = FALSE, aic = FALSE, confint = 0.95,
                  x = TRUE)

# Results
wce_gpu
summary(wce_gpu)

# See estimated weight function
plot(wce_gpu)

# Bootstrap-based inference, as a separate step (example with 20
# replicates, but normally R > 500)
wce_gpu_bootstrap <- bootstrap(wce_gpu, R = 20)

# See confidence bands for the estimated weight function due to bootstrap
plot(wce_gpu_bootstrap)

# All estimated coefficients in bootstrap
coef(wce_gpu_bootstrap)

# Estimate a HR (Exposed at a dose vs. unexposed)
exposed   <- rep(1, 90)
unexposed <- rep(0, 90)

HR(wce_gpu_bootstrap, exposed, unexposed)
} # }
